topic: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
usual_baseline: Low. Only 13.9% of hip fractures assessed for bone protection [1397]. Treatment started in 16% of hip and 0% of wrist fractures [1193]. 5 of 38 fracture clinic patients referred [1223]. 27.6% of women with low-trauma fracture on therapy [1234]. 0% FRAX in psychiatric inpatients [1146]. FLS referral 5% [1420]. 87% not started on bisphosphonates by GP [1477].
fix_that_works: Giving the care of the elderly team ownership: 13.9% to 100%, sustained a year on [1397]. Community fracture liaison nurse: bone-sparing agent 39.5% to 70.5% in over-75s [1296]. Kardex stickers: 50.9% to 84.6% [1249]. Ward round template: FRAX 50% to 88% [1165]. Protocol: any treatment 36% to 58% [1210]. MRS BAD BONES mnemonic: bone-sparing drugs 18.2% to 72.4% [1380].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, MDTs and new roles: 64% still without bisphosphonates and FRAX fell 54% to 18% [1477]. Awareness alone: 5/38 to 23/43 referred [1223]; 60% still not sent for DEXA [1218]. Rewritten GP letter: 40% to 51% [1168]. Posters alone reached 44.4% [1397]. No high-risk patient started a bisphosphonate after the template [1165]. EHR alert: 5% to 19% only [1420].
consultant_advice: Heavily audited and the answer repeats: teaching barely moves it, giving a named team or nurse ownership does. Don't measure prescribing at discharge again. Measure whether patients are still on treatment a year on, where adherence was 11.6% [1550], or whether GPs start what was recommended.
